Half of UK Adults Unclear on Making Tax Digital, New Wolters Kluwer Research Finds
summary:
Half of UK adults (50%) don’t know what Making Tax Digital (MTD) for Income Tax involves, according to new research commissioned by Wolters Kluwer Tax & Accounting. Almost a third (31%) have never heard of MTD, and a further 19% have heard of it but don’t know what it involves. The findings come as sole traders and landlords already using MTD prepare to send HMRC their next quarterly update, due by 7 November.
MTD is the biggest change to how income tax is reported since Self Assessment. Instead of reporting once a year, sole traders and landlords keep digital records and send HMRC a summary of their income and expenses every three months. Those with qualifying income over £50,000 have been required to use MTD since April 2026. The threshold falls to £30,000 from April 2027 and is planned to fall to £20,000 from April 2028, bringing many more people into scope.
“Making Tax Digital is here, and for many people it is closer than they think. Our research shows that a lot of people still don’t know what it involves, or whether it applies to them. The good news is that it is not too late. With the next group of landlords and sole traders joining in April 2027, now is the time to check whether you are in scope, choose the right tool, and start keeping records as you go. Accountants have a central role to play in helping their clients make that change with confidence,” said Bas Kniphorst, EVP and Managing Director of Wolters Kluwer Tax & Accounting Europe.
Awareness is not the same as understanding

Confidence is also low. More than half (51%) are not confident they would know if a change to tax rules, such as MTD, applied to them, including 22% who are not at all confident. Just 11% say they are very confident.
Many rely on reminders to meet tax deadlines

People also turn to others for support. Around one in seven (15%) have asked a family member, friend or colleague for help with a tax deadline, while 11% have paid an accountant to sort it out for them.
Record keeping remains a weak spot


“Making Tax Digital is a real opportunity for sole traders and landlords to move their finances online. The start is the hardest part, but once you choose the right tool and log your income and expenses as you go, each quarterly update gets easier. Digital records often mean fewer mistakes, less time chasing receipts and a clear, up-to-date view of how your business is doing throughout the year, not just at tax time. Accountants have a big role to play here. They can help clients make the switch and turn those regular updates into timely advice that helps them run their business with more confidence,” said Marie Costers, VP & General Manager, Wolters Kluwer Tax & Accounting Belgium, the Netherlands and the UK.
Preparation still matters

content: New research by Wolters Kluwer reveals that half of UK adults are unclear about Making Tax Digital (MTD) for Income Tax, with nearly a third having never heard of it. The findings highlight low awareness and confidence among taxpayers as sole traders and landlords prepare for upcoming deadlines and phased implementation thresholds through 2028.

Flexys Partners With The Very Group on Customer Support Technology
summary:
Flexys, a provider of technology for supporting customers in arrears or financial difficulty, announces a partnership with The Very Group to enhance the technology used to help those who fall behind on payments, helping them to get back on track with the right support at the right time.
The software will give The Very Group’s teams a real-time, complete view of each customer's situation, so they can make more informed decisions, respond to individual circumstances and offer suitable, affordable options. 
With the partnership, Flexys will provide:
a complete, real-time view of each customer's account, so teams can tailor their response to individual circumstances
one place for advisers and strategy teams to see the full picture and act on it
affordability tools built in, to help agree repayment plans customers can genuinely sustain
automation that handles routine steps, freeing advisers to spend time with the customers who need more help
reporting built on real-time data, so the business can see how well customers are being supported
The software is designed with FCA Consumer Duty in mind, helping The Very Group evidence that it delivers good outcomes for customers who find themselves in difficulty.
James Hill, CEO of Flexys, said: "Our partnership with The Very Group reflects our commitment to helping financial services providers deliver more effective, personalised customer support through technology. Our software is designed to make it easier to understand individual circumstances, provide appropriate support and give customers greater flexibility in how they manage their finances."
The project reflects where the industry is heading. Under FCA Consumer Duty, lenders and credit providers are expected to show they deliver good outcomes for customers in difficulty. More are now moving to modern, cloud-native software that puts each customer's circumstances, real-time information and affordability at the centre of the support they offer.

content: Flexys has partnered with The Very Group to enhance customer support technology for individuals experiencing financial difficulty. The software provides a real-time view of customer accounts, built-in affordability tools, and automation to help advisers offer tailored repayment plans. Designed to align with FCA Consumer Duty regulations, the collaboration aims to improve support outcomes for customers falling behind on payments.
